# RFC-0001 Feature Demo Generator — Independent Research Assessment

**Model role:** Independent commission member. I have not seen other models' outputs and treat none as verification.

**Critical evidence constraint:** I have no live web/search access in this session. What follows is drawn from (a) the RFC itself, (b) my training-data knowledge of the tools and product categories named, and (c) reasoning from first principles. Wherever a claim depends on a specific product feature, pricing, API surface, or "does X exist today," I mark it **[UNVERIFIED — needs live check]**. This is a substantial limitation and I flag it up front rather than fabricating citations.

---

## 1. Executive Conclusion

**The wedge is real but narrow, and it is not where the RFC's language suggests.** The novel, defensible seam is not "generate a demo" (crowded) and not "summarize a PR" (very crowded). It is the **specific join** between:

1. a merge-triggered repo interrogation that identifies the *user-visible surface* of a change, and
2. a sub-two-minute structured product-context interview captured *while the author still has it in their head*, and
3. a **demo spec** (structured intermediate representation) from which scripts, screenshots, recorded walkthroughs, and narrated videos are all rendered.

The interview + demo-spec + multi-renderer axis is where I see the least direct prior art. The "PR → summary" half and the "interactive demo builder" half are each extremely well served. **[INFERENCE, medium confidence]** No product I am aware of connects a git merge event through a structured PM-interview to a multi-format demo artifact as a single flow — but I cannot rule out an internal tool at a large company or a recent 2025 launch I don't have visibility on. **[UNVERIFIED]**

**Recommendation:** Conditional GO on a tightly scoped MVP that produces **only** demo scripts (not video) from **only** merged PRs on **only** web-app repos, with the interview as the hero UX. Defer capture/video entirely to Phase 2. Kill criteria in §10.

**Strongest argument against building it (stated up front):** The output of a good PR summary bot plus a five-minute Loom is already "good enough" for most teams, and the teams disciplined enough to run a two-minute interview on every merge are already disciplined enough to write a demo. The tool may be solving a discipline problem with technology, which historically fails. See §11.

---

## 2. Market & Prior-Art Map

I group the landscape into six adjacent categories. For each I note what it does well and what it does *not* do that the RFC requires.

### 2.1 PR / commit intelligence and AI changelog
- **GitHub Copilot PR summaries, CodeRabbit, Graphite Reviewer, Greptile, What The Diff, Ellipsis, Codegen, Aviator** — all generate PR descriptions, reviews, or changelog text from diffs. **[UNVERIFIED specifics per product]**
- **Release-note / changelog generators**: release-please, semantic-release, git-cliff, Changie, Beamer, LaunchNotes, Herald. Focused on the "*what shipped*" text artifact.
- **Gap vs. RFC:** These stop at *text about the code*. None (that I know of) elicit product-context from the author or produce a runnable/screenable demo. **[INFERENCE]**

### 2.2 Interactive demo / product-tour builders
- **Arcade, Supademo, Storylane, Navattic, Reprise, Tourial, Walnut** — capture click-flows in a browser, produce interactive HTML demos with hotspots and branching.
- **Gap vs. RFC:** Human-driven capture. No merge trigger. No repo awareness. Marketing/sales-owned, not engineering-owned. **[reasonable confidence, UNVERIFIED per current feature set]**

### 2.3 Screen recording & narrated how-to
- **Loom, Tella, Scribe, Guidde, Descript, Screen Studio, Vidyard.**
- **Guidde** and **Scribe** auto-generate step docs and voiceover from a capture. **Descript** does script-driven video editing with TTS.
- **Gap:** Still human-initiated capture; no code-side triggering; no product-context interview.

### 2.4 Browser / UI automation (potential capture engine)
- **Playwright, Puppeteer, Cypress, Selenium** for scripted UI drive.
- **Playwright's `codegen`** and **trace viewer** can record actions.
- **Chromatic, Percy, Argos** — visual regression tools that already screenshot component/story states on every PR. **This is a genuinely under-appreciated adjacency for the MVP.** [INFERENCE, medium confidence]
- **Storybook + Chromatic**: component stories rendered per commit, screenshotted, diffed. If the changed surface has a Story, you already have a before/after screenshot for free.
- **Browser-use, Anthropic Computer Use, Skyvern, OpenAI Operator** — agentic browser drivers. **[UNVERIFIED — capability & reliability for demo-quality capture as of now]**

### 2.5 CI/CD integration points
- **GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Buildkite** — standard triggers on merge to main.
- **Danger.js / Danger Systems** — the canonical "run stuff on a PR and comment back" framework. Directly relevant scaffolding.

### 2.6 Narrated-video generation
- **ElevenLabs, PlayHT, OpenAI TTS, Azure Neural TTS** — TTS quality is now demo-acceptable for most enterprise use.
- **Synthesia, HeyGen, Descript** — script → video pipelines, mostly with avatars, not screen captures.
- **Gap:** None (that I know of) take a *diff + interview* as input.

### 2.7 The specific intersection the RFC targets
**[INFERENCE, medium confidence]** I am not aware of a shipping product whose primary flow is "merge event → repo interrogation → PM interview → demo artifact." I know of:
- internal "demo bot" mentions in engineering blogs at consumer companies (rare, ad hoc) **[UNVERIFIED]**
- DX/DevRel tooling (Docusaurus, Mintlify, Fern) that auto-updates docs from code but not demos
- **Mintlify** and **Fern** have moved toward "AI-authored docs from code" — closest neighbor on the docs axis, not the demo axis. **[UNVERIFIED — current scope]**

**Missing evidence I would want to verify with live search:**
- Any 2024–2026 YC batch entrants in "AI demo from code"
- Internal tools at Vercel, Linear, Stripe, GitHub, Notion, Figma described in engineering blogs
- Whether Supademo/Arcade have added git integrations
- Whether Chromatic has moved beyond visual regression into narrated flows

---

## 3. Feature-by-Feature Competitor Matrix

Columns: (A) merge-triggered, (B) reads diff/PR, (C) elicits PM context from human, (D) produces demo script, (E) produces annotated screenshots, (F) produces recorded video, (G) produces narrated video, (H) engineer-owned workflow.

| Product / Category | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CodeRabbit / Copilot PR / Greptile | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | partial (text) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| release-please / git-cliff | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ (notes only) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| LaunchNotes / Beamer | ✗ | ✗ | partial (notes UI) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Arcade / Supademo / Storylane | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | partial | ✗ |
| Guidde / Scribe | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ (from capture) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Loom / Tella / Descript | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ (Descript) | ✗ |
| Chromatic / Percy | ✓ | ✓ (visual) | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ (raw) | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Playwright codegen + traces | manual | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Synthesia / HeyGen | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Mintlify / Fern (docs) | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| **RFC-0001 target** | **✓** | **✓** | **✓** | **✓** | **✓** | **✓** | **✓** | **✓** |

**[All matrix cells UNVERIFIED against current product docs]** — treat as directional. The pattern is what matters: column C (product-context interview tied to a code event) is empty everywhere I look.

---

## 4. Technical Architecture Comparison

### 4.1 The three architectures to weigh

**A. CI-triggered, fully headless.**
Merge fires GitHub Action → job clones repo, computes diff, queries LLM, posts a "please answer these 5 questions" comment on the merged PR or a Slack DM → on answer, produces script and optionally kicks off headless Playwright capture against a preview deployment.

- *Strength:* Never skipped. Runs on 100% of merges.
- *Weakness:* Headless capture against a live app is the hardest part of this whole idea. Auth, seed data, feature flags, and non-deterministic UI make it fragile. The RFC correctly flags this.
- *Feasibility:* Text artifacts — high. Screenshot/video — low to medium, and only if a Storybook/preview-deploy contract exists.

**B. Editor/agent-based, interactive.**
Invoked in Cursor/VS Code/CLI right after merge; conversational interview; capture uses the developer's already-running app.

- *Strength:* Live UI capture is trivial when a human is already driving it. Interview is conversational.
- *Weakness:* Depends on human invocation. Reintroduces the exact "extra step that gets skipped" that the RFC is trying to solve.
- *Feasibility:* High for text and screenshots; medium for video (needs OS-level capture or browser-extension capture).

**C. Hybrid — recommended.**
CI does Pass 1 (repo interrogation) and drafts the interview automatically on merge → author is pinged (Slack + PR comment) with a link to a two-minute pre-filled form → **script is produced with zero further human effort** → optional capture pass is a separate, deferrable action taken later by the author or a designated demo-owner, in their editor or against a preview deploy.

- *This decomposes the failure surface.* Script generation (high value, low fragility) becomes the always-on artifact. Capture (high fragility) becomes opt-in and can fail without breaking the primary flow.
- Matches the RFC's own conclusion that "the demo script is the natural intermediate representation."

### 4.2 Where the pipeline actually breaks

Ranked by risk:

1. **Identifying the user-visible surface** from a diff. Backend refactors, dependency bumps, and internal-tool changes will trip a naive "look at changed files" heuristic. Need a classifier or explicit `demo:` PR label. **[INFERENCE]**
2. **Grounding pre-filled answers.** Hallucinated "customer / benefit / replaces" content is the failure mode that will destroy trust fastest. The pre-fill must visibly cite its sources (linked ticket, PR body, commit message) or explicitly say "I couldn't guess this — you tell me."
3. **Auth + seed data** for headless capture. Almost every non-trivial SaaS demo needs a logged-in state with meaningful data. This is a per-customer integration problem, not a product problem you solve once.
4. **UI-action mapping.** Turning "in the script, click the Export button" into a reliable Playwright selector requires either (a) a stable data-testid convention, (b) vision-model-driven action grounding, or (c) Storybook stories as capture surfaces. Storybook is by far the cheapest path where it applies. **[INFERENCE]**
5. **Interview fatigue.** Firing on every merge is wrong. Needs a gate: PR label (`demo`), size heuristic (touches UI files above threshold), or explicit opt-in per PR.

---

## 5. Build-versus-Integrate Analysis

**Build in-house:**
- The **demo spec** (data model). Nobody else has one shaped like this and it is the crown jewel.
- The **interview UX** and its pre-fill logic.
- The **merge-trigger orchestration** and the "is this demo-worthy" gate.
- The **script-generation prompt chain** (repo facts + interview → structured beats).

**Integrate / buy:**
- **LLM:** Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, or open-weights via Bedrock/Vertex. Do not train.
- **Repo interrogation:** GitHub REST/GraphQL API + `git` locally. Optionally layer on **Greptile** or **Sourcegraph Cody** for code-semantic search. **[UNVERIFIED pricing/API]**
- **Browser automation:** **Playwright** (do not build).
- **Screenshot rendering surface:** if the customer has Storybook, use it. Otherwise Playwright against preview deployments (Vercel, Netlify, Render preview URLs).
- **Video assembly:** **Remotion** (React-based programmatic video) or **FFmpeg** direct. Remotion is the strongest fit because your intermediate is a structured script.
- **TTS:** **ElevenLabs** or **OpenAI TTS**. Do not build.
- **Delivery:** post as PR comment (GitHub API), Slack message (Slack API), or a hosted viewer page.

**Don't build:** capture-only tooling, TTS, video encoding, LLM inference, general PR summarization.

**The uncomfortable integrate question:** could this be built as **a layer on top of Supademo or Arcade** rather than a standalone product? A "Supademo trigger from GitHub" plugin would capture much of the value if their APIs allow programmatic demo creation. **[UNVERIFIED — need to check their APIs]**. If yes, the standalone-product thesis weakens meaningfully.

---

## 6. Interview UX Recommendation

The interview is the product. Get this right and the rest is plumbing.

**Principles:**
- **Never a blank field.** Every question is pre-filled with a best-guess draft or an honest "I couldn't infer this."
- **Show your work.** Each pre-filled answer shows the source: "drafted from linked ticket LIN-4421" or "drafted from PR title."
- **One screen, five questions, two minutes.** Anything longer and it becomes the skipped step.
- **Structured output, not prose.** The interview writes to a schema (see §7), not a freeform textbox. This is what lets script generation be deterministic-ish.
- **Deliverable within the tools they already use.** PR comment → clickable link → hosted form → submit posts back to PR. Do not require a new login where avoidable. GitHub OAuth is fine.
- **Editable after the fact.** The demo spec is a persistent artifact that can be reopened and refined; the "interview" is really the initial capture.

**Question set (tightened from RFC):**
1. **Use case** — When would someone reach for this? *(pre-filled from linked issue title / PR body)*
2. **Who's the customer?** — Persona or named account. *(pre-filled: "I couldn't infer — you tell me" unless a persona keyword appears)*
3. **Outcome** — What can they now do that they couldn't before? *(pre-filled from PR title verb + changed surface)*
4. **Benefit** — Time / risk / revenue / delight. *(radio-select + one line, not free text — this is the highest-hallucination-risk field)*
5. **Replaces what?** — Manual process, competitor, prior version. *(pre-filled "unknown" — force the human)*

**Deliberate anti-pattern to avoid:** Do NOT let the LLM guess the "benefit" and "customer" confidently. The tool's credibility dies the first time it invents a customer segment. Prefer "I don't know — you tell me" over confident wrongness. **[INFERENCE, high conviction]**

**Optional follow-ups (collapsed by default):** the "oh, that's cool" moment; caveats; who not to show yet.

---

## 7. Proposed Demo Spec Data Model

The core artifact. Everything else is a renderer on top of this.

```yaml
demo_spec:
  id: ds_2026_08_pr_1421
  version: 1
  source:
    repo: acme/product
    pr: 1421
    merge_sha: 9f2a...
    merged_at: 2026-08-01T14:22Z
    trigger: merge_to_main | manual | scheduled
  repo_facts:                       # Pass 1, automatic
    scope_prs: [1421]
    surfaces_changed: [ui, api]     # classified
    files:
      - path: web/src/Export.tsx
        role: primary_ui
      - path: api/export.py
        role: backend
    tests_added: [web/src/Export.test.tsx]
    docs_touched: []
    linked_issues: [LIN-4421]
    pr_title: "Add CSV export to reports"
    pr_body_summary: "..."
    change_kind: net_new | iteration | fix | refactor
    is_user_visible: true           # gating classifier
  product_context:                  # Pass 2, from interview
    use_case: {value: "...", source: draft_from_linked_issue, confirmed: true}
    customer: {value: "...", source: human, confirmed: true}
    outcome: {value: "...", source: draft_from_pr_title, confirmed: true}
    benefit: {category: time_saved, detail: "...", confirmed: true}
    replaces: {value: "...", source: human, confirmed: true}
    coolness_moment: null
    caveats: []
    do_not_show: false
  script:                           # generated
    title: "CSV export in Reports"
    hook: "..."
    beats:
      - action: navigate
        target: "/reports"
        selector_hint: "reports nav item"
        say: "Start on the reports page..."
        why_it_matters: "..."
      - action: click
        target: "Export"
        selector_hint: "button[data-testid=export]"
        say: "..."
      - action: assert_visible
        target: "download started toast"
  renderers:
    - kind: script_markdown, status: ready, url: ...
    - kind: screenshots, status: pending
    - kind: recorded_video, status: not_requested
    - kind: narrated_video, status: not_requested
  distribution:
    pr_comment_id: 998877
    slack_message_ts: null
```

Key design choices:
- **Every field carries provenance** (`source`, `confirmed`) so we can display "drafted from X" in the UI and never lose the audit trail.
- **Beats are structured actions**, not prose. This is what makes multi-renderer feasible.
- **Selector hints, not selectors.** The renderer resolves against the actual app; the spec stays app-agnostic.

---

## 8. Phased MVP & Experiments

### Phase 0 (2 weeks) — Discovery, not build
- 10 interviews with target users: engineers who recently landed a demo-worthy feature, PMs/DevRel who consume demos.
- Ask what they do today, how long it takes, what "good" looks like, whether they'd install a GitHub App for this.
- Look at 50 recently merged PRs from 3–5 friendly repos and hand-classify: how many are demo-worthy? How much of the interview could a human fill in from PR+ticket alone?

**Kill signal:** if fewer than ~15–20% of merges are demo-worthy AND the target users describe the current pain as "annoying but not urgent," the automatic-trigger thesis is fragile. Consider pivoting to explicit-invocation only.

### Phase 1 (4–6 weeks) — Script-only, hybrid architecture
- GitHub App that posts a "demo interview" comment on merged PRs matching a gate (label `demo` OR touches UI files above threshold).
- Hosted interview form, five questions, pre-filled with LLM drafts.
- On submit: produce a markdown demo script, post back as PR comment; also emit the demo spec JSON.
- **No capture. No video. No screenshots.**
- Target: 3 pilot teams, 4 weeks of usage.

**Success signals to advance:**
- ≥60% of triggered PRs complete the interview
- ≥50% of resulting scripts are used downstream (linked in Slack, changelog, or sales enablement — measurable via link telemetry)
- Median interview time under 3 minutes
- Qualitative: "I would be sad if this went away"

### Phase 2 (6–8 weeks) — Add screenshots via Storybook or preview deploys
- If the repo has Storybook, hook into it (find stories touched by the diff, screenshot them) — highest leverage.
- Otherwise, Playwright against Vercel/Netlify preview URLs, driven by the script's beats. Expect this to be flaky for the first two design partners; that is data, not failure.
- Do not attempt capture on repos without a preview-deploy or Storybook contract. Say "sorry, unsupported."

### Phase 3 (open-ended) — Recorded video, then narrated video
- Recorded: Playwright + FFmpeg from the script beats.
- Narrated: Remotion + ElevenLabs.
- Only build after Phase 2 stabilizes; the fragility curve is steep.

### Experiments to run in parallel
- **E1: Pre-fill quality.** Blind-rate 30 pre-filled interviews on customer/benefit/outcome for hallucination rate. If >15% confident-wrong, tighten prompting to prefer "unknown."
- **E2: Trigger gating.** Compare a label-based trigger vs. a heuristic (UI files touched, non-trivial diff) on false-positive rate.
- **E3: Distribution channel A/B.** PR comment vs. Slack DM vs. both. Measure interview completion.
- **E4: Author vs. reviewer.** Does the interview work better when addressed to the PR author, or to a designated demo-owner? The RFC assumes author; that assumption deserves testing.

---

## 9. Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interview fatigue → rubber-stamping | High | High | Gate hard; don't fire on every merge; measure completion quality not just rate |
| Confident-wrong pre-fills destroy trust | High | Very high | Show provenance; prefer "unknown"; UX makes overwriting easier than confirming |
| Capture fragility (auth, seed data, flakiness) | Very high | Medium | Defer to Phase 2; only support Storybook/preview-deploy contracts; degrade gracefully to script-only |
| Discipline problem masquerading as tech problem | Medium | Very high | See §11 |
| Adjacent products add merge triggers first | Medium | High | Ship the interview + spec quickly; that's the moat, not the automation |
| Enterprise procurement + GitHub App permissions | Medium | Medium | Design for self-hosted / bring-your-own-LLM-key from day one |
| Distribution: demos generated but unused | High | Very high | Measure downstream reuse explicitly; if <30% by Phase 1 end, the problem statement is wrong |
| Backend/refactor/infra PRs will dominate merges | Very high | Medium | Gating classifier for "is this user-visible" is non-optional |
| LLM cost per merge at scale | Low | Low | Cheap for reasonable-sized diffs; cap by size |

---

## 10. Decision Criteria (Go / No-Go)

**GO if, after Phase 0 discovery:**
- ≥7 of 10 interviewees describe the pain in unprompted terms consistent with the RFC
- ≥3 teams commit to a Phase 1 pilot
- Hand-classification shows ≥20% of merges are demo-worthy in target repos
- No incumbent identified doing merge-triggered PM interview → demo spec

**GO to Phase 2 if, after Phase 1:**
- ≥60% interview completion
- ≥50% downstream reuse
- ≥1 pilot team says they'd pay
- Script quality "sendable with light edits" on ≥70% of outputs (rated by consuming PMs/DevRel, not by us)

**NO-GO / pivot signals:**
- Interview completion <40% — pain not real enough
- Scripts generated but unused — the artifact isn't the problem
- Users ignore pre-fills and rewrite from scratch — the interrogation half isn't adding value
- A funded incumbent ships the same wedge during Phase 1 — reassess as an integration play

---

## 11. Strongest Argument Against Building It

**The RFC diagnoses a symptom (demos don't get made) and attributes it to a friction problem (extra work, knowledge decay). But the underlying cause may be a prioritization problem: demos don't get made because nobody's job depends on them getting made.**

If that's the real cause, then:
- A two-minute interview will be skipped by the same people who skip writing a good PR description today.
- Pre-filled forms will get rubber-stamped, producing a firehose of low-quality "demos" that erode trust faster than no demos would.
- The teams that adopt this tool will be the teams that were already going to make demos — the tool captures existing behavior, not new behavior.
- A well-run team with a "no merge without a demo" norm and a Loom account beats a poorly-run team with this tool.

Corroborating evidence for this reading:
- Documentation tools have existed for decades; documentation quality correlates with team culture, not tooling.
- Test coverage tools didn't create testing cultures; they measured existing ones.
- The RFC's own Risks section flags "interview fatigue" and "generated demos that don't get distributed" — those aren't edge cases, those are the modal outcome if the diagnosis is wrong.

**The counter-argument (why to build anyway):** The pre-filled draft materially changes the effort curve. Going from "write a demo from scratch" (30–90 min) to "confirm five pre-filled answers" (2 min) is a genuine order-of-magnitude reduction, and order-of-magnitude effort reductions do shift behavior even in disciplined-vs.-undisciplined teams. This is testable in Phase 0. Do the test before committing to Phase 1.

---

Technical Architecture Comparison\n\n### 4.1 The three architectures to weigh\n\n**A. CI-triggered, fully headless.**\nMerge fires GitHub Action → job clones repo, computes diff, queries LLM, posts a \"please answer these 5 questions\" comment on the merged PR or a Slack DM → on answer, produces script and optionally kicks off headless Playwright capture against a preview deployment.\n\n- *Strength:* Never skipped. Runs on 100% of merges.\n- *Weakness:* Headless capture against a live app is the hardest part of this whole idea. Auth, seed data, feature flags, and non-deterministic UI make it fragile. The RFC correctly flags this.\n- *Feasibility:* Text artifacts — high. Screenshot/video — low to medium, and only if a Storybook/preview-deploy contract exists.\n\n**B. Editor/agent-based, interactive.**\nInvoked in Cursor/VS Code/CLI right after merge; conversational interview; capture uses the developer's already-running app.\n\n- *Strength:* Live UI capture is trivial when a human is already driving it. Interview is conversational.\n- *Weakness:* Depends on human invocation. Reintroduces the exact \"extra step that gets skipped\" that the RFC is trying to solve.\n- *Feasibility:* High for text and screenshots; medium for video (needs OS-level capture or browser-extension capture).\n\n**C. Hybrid — recommended.**\nCI does Pass 1 (repo interrogation) and drafts the interview automatically on merge → author is pinged (Slack + PR comment) with a link to a two-minute pre-filled form → **script is produced with zero further human effort** → optional capture pass is a separate, deferrable action taken later by the author or a designated demo-owner, in their editor or against a preview deploy.\n\n- *This decomposes the failure surface.* Script generation (high value, low fragility) becomes the always-on artifact. Capture (high fragility) becomes opt-in and can fail without breaking the primary flow.\n- Matches the RFC's own conclusion that \"the demo script is the natural intermediate representation.\"\n\n### 4.2 Where the pipeline actually breaks\n\nRanked by risk:\n\n1. **Identifying the user-visible surface** from a diff. Backend refactors, dependency bumps, and internal-tool changes will trip a naive \"look at changed files\" heuristic. Need a classifier or explicit `demo:` PR label. **[INFERENCE]**\n2. **Grounding pre-filled answers.** Hallucinated \"customer / benefit / replaces\" content is the failure mode that will destroy trust fastest. The pre-fill must visibly cite its sources (linked ticket, PR body, commit message) or explicitly say \"I couldn't guess this — you tell me.\"\n3. **Auth + seed data** for headless capture. Almost every non-trivial SaaS demo needs a logged-in state with meaningful data. This is a per-customer integration problem, not a product problem you solve once.\n4. **UI-action mapping.** Turning \"in the script, click the Export button\" into a reliable Playwright selector requires either (a) a stable data-testid convention, (b) vision-model-driven action grounding, or (c) Storybook stories as capture surfaces. Storybook is by far the cheapest path where it applies. **[INFERENCE]**\n5. **Interview fatigue.** Firing on every merge is wrong. Needs a gate: PR label (`demo`), size heuristic (touches UI files above threshold), or explicit opt-in per PR.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Get this right and the rest is plumbing.\n\n**Principles:**\n- **Never a blank field.** Every question is pre-filled with a best-guess draft or an honest \"I couldn't infer this.\"\n- **Show your work.** Each pre-filled answer shows the source: \"drafted from linked ticket LIN-4421\" or \"drafted from PR title.\"\n- **One screen, five questions, two minutes.** Anything longer and it becomes the skipped step.\n- **Structured output, not prose.** The interview writes to a schema (see §7), not a freeform textbox. This is what lets script generation be deterministic-ish.\n- **Deliverable within the tools they already use.** PR comment → clickable link → hosted form → submit posts back to PR. Do not require a new login where avoidable. GitHub OAuth is fine.\n- **Editable after the fact.** The demo spec is a persistent artifact that can be reopened and refined; the \"interview\" is really the initial capture.\n\n**Question set (tightened from RFC):**\n1. **Use case** — When would someone reach for this? *(pre-filled from linked issue title / PR body)*\n2. **Who's the customer?** — Persona or named account. *(pre-filled: \"I couldn't infer — you tell me\" unless a persona keyword appears)*\n3. **Outcome** — What can they now do that they couldn't before? *(pre-filled from PR title verb + changed surface)*\n4. **Benefit** — Time / risk / revenue / delight. *(radio-select + one line, not free text — this is the highest-hallucination-risk field)*\n5. **Replaces what?** — Manual process, competitor, prior version. *(pre-filled \"unknown\" — force the human)*\n\n**Deliberate anti-pattern to avoid:** Do NOT let the LLM guess the \"benefit\" and \"customer\" confidently. The tool's credibility dies the first time it invents a customer segment. Prefer \"I don't know — you tell me\" over confident wrongness. **[INFERENCE, high conviction]**\n\n**Optional follow-ups (collapsed by default):** the \"oh, that's cool\" moment; caveats; who not to show yet.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Phased MVP & Experiments\n\n### Phase 0 (2 weeks) — Discovery, not build\n- 10 interviews with target users: engineers who recently landed a demo-worthy feature, PMs/DevRel who consume demos.\n- Ask what they do today, how long it takes, what \"good\" looks like, whether they'd install a GitHub App for this.\n- Look at 50 recently merged PRs from 3–5 friendly repos and hand-classify: how many are demo-worthy? Strongest Argument Against Building It\n\n**The RFC diagnoses a symptom (demos don't get made) and attributes it to a friction problem (extra work, knowledge decay). But the underlying cause may be a prioritization problem: demos don't get made because nobody's job depends on them getting made.**\n\nIf that's the real cause, then:\n- A two-minute interview will be skipped by the same people who skip writing a good PR description today.\n- Pre-filled forms will get rubber-stamped, producing a firehose of low-quality \"demos\" that erode trust faster than no demos would.\n- The teams that adopt this tool will be the teams that were already going to make demos — the tool captures existing behavior, not new behavior.\n- A well-run team with a \"no merge without a demo\" norm and a Loom account beats a poorly-run team with this tool.\n\nCorroborating evidence for this reading:\n- Documentation tools have existed for decades; documentation quality correlates with team culture, not tooling.\n- Test coverage tools didn't create testing cultures; they measured existing ones.\n- The RFC's own Risks section flags \"interview fatigue\" and \"generated demos that don't get distributed\" — those aren't edge cases, those are the modal outcome if the diagnosis is wrong.\n\n**The counter-argument (why to build anyway):** The pre-filled draft materially changes the effort curve. Going from \"write a demo from scratch\" (30–90 min) to \"confirm five pre-filled answers\" (2 min) is a genuine order-of-magnitude reduction, and order-of-magnitude effort reductions do shift behavior even in disciplined-vs.-undisciplined teams.
